title: The Casual Surge Gap: Why a Recruitment Firm's Biggest Placement Month Is Its Tightest Month for Cash
linkedin:
November is the best month on the board for a lot of recruitment and labour hire desks. Christmas placements are flooding in across retail, hospitality, warehousing and logistics.

It is also, almost every single year, the tightest month those same businesses have for cash.

Here is why. Every placement creates a wage obligation that is due weekly or fortnightly, no matter what. The invoice to the host client for that same placement is rarely paid in under thirty to sixty days. Double your placement volume into December and you have not doubled your cash cushion. You have doubled the number of wage payments you are funding before the matching invoices clear.

Host clients, especially the larger retail and warehouse operators, set payment terms to suit their own cash cycle. Those terms do not move just because your volume tripled for six weeks. In Queensland, Victoria and South Australia there is also the ongoing cost of a labour hire licence sitting on top of that funding gap.

The desks that handle this well are not the highest margin ones. They are the ones who modelled the gap back in October, before the surge, rather than discovering it in the second week of December when a facility increase takes weeks to arrange and a bank has little patience for a request made under pressure.
